title: Joint Time Delay and Doppler Passive Acoustic 3D Tracking of Bats
author: Ales Mishchenko
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.iyjcfun

steps.title: Prepare Ultrasonic Microphones
steps.instruction: Select 4 ultrasonic microphones capable of recording the ultrasound range of the target bat species. Microphones with peak sensitivity between 30 kHz to 60 kHz (e.g., Knowles acoustics model SPM0204UD5) are recommended.

steps.title: Construct Microphone Antenna
steps.instruction: Construct an antenna to hold the 4 microphones in a regular tetrahedron (pyramidal) configuration with a side length of 1-2m. Attach microphones and orient them toward the expected bat location. (Note: A 1.2m antenna was used for SPM0204UD5 microphones).

steps.title: Record Bat Calls
steps.instruction: Install the antenna at the recording site, connect microphones to a computer, and record an 'all-record' file for the duration necessary to capture the planned number of bats. Note the time of typical bat appearances.

steps.title: Estimate Signal and Noise Levels
steps.instruction: Locate a typical bat recording within the 'all-record' file and use sound processing software (e.g., Matlab, Audacity) to estimate typical noise and typical bat-call signal levels.

steps.title: Extract Recording Segments
steps.instruction: Use a script (e.g., Matlab) to automatically extract short (2-4sec) 'recordings' from the 'all-record' file where the signal exceeds the average of the typical noise and typical signal levels.

substeps.instruction: Filter the 'all-record' to retain only frequencies near the peak intensity of the target bats.
If recording many bats, use frequencies above 30 kHz to filter out low-frequency noise (e.g., insects, cars).

steps.title: Segment Recordings and Calculate TDOAmax
steps.instruction: Split each detected recording into time-segments (dt) containing an average of 2 to 3 bat calls. If the time-lag between subsequent calls is unknown, assume a lag between 60ms and 100ms.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the maximum possible TDOA (TDOAmax = antenna size / sound speed). For a 1.2m antenna, TDOAmax is < 5ms, allowing a time-segment length of 185ms to contain 2-3 calls on average.

steps.title: Calculate Spectral Density and Spectrograms
steps.instruction: For each time-segment, calculate the amplitude spectral density ASD(t) and the spectrogram SG(t).

steps.title: Compute Cross-Correlations
steps.instruction: Calculate the cross-correlation of S(t), ASD(t), and SG(t) between all pairs of microphones (i,j): xcorr(t)(Si,Sj), xcorr(t)(ASDi,ASDj), and xcorr(t)(SGi,SGj).

steps.title: Filter TFDOA-set
steps.instruction: Identify the M highest cross-correlation maximums to use as the TFDOA(t)-set for the system (5) from the referenced PLoS-ONE paper. For recordings with one echo, M=6 is effective; for cluttered or noisy environments, test M > 6.

substeps.instruction: Assign arguments of maximums of xcorr(t)(Si,Sj), xcorr(t)(ASDi,ASDj), and xcorr(t)(SGi,SGj) as TDOA1j(t), FDOA2j(t), and TDOA3j(t), FDOA3j(t) respectively.

steps.title: Determine Consistent TFDOA
steps.instruction: For each time t, select the 'most consistent' TFDOA(t) from the TFDOA(t)-set that satisfies equations (5) from the PLoS-ONE paper with the smallest residue.

steps.title: Reconstruct Missing TFDOAs
steps.instruction: If insufficient data (cross-correlation maximums above noise level) exists for some time-segments t, use system (5) to reconstruct TFDOA(t) from TFDOA(t+dt) and/or TFDOA(t-dt).

substeps.instruction: Calculate the confidence of the reconstruction using the procedure in the 'The confidence of reconstruction of missing TDOAs' subsection of the PLoS-ONE paper.
Repeat this process until no further TFDOAs(t) can be reconstructed using available TFDOA(t+dt) and TFDOA(t-dt).

steps.title: Calculate Bat Locations
steps.instruction: Use the calculated TFDOA(t) to determine bat locations x(t) using optimization methods, such as the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm implemented in the Matlab nonlinear least-squares solver.
